- 2026-09-17T15:09:57.567Z — rule: **Take the run lock with flock semantics only — never fcntl/lockf, SQLite locks, sockets or pid files — so Node, Rust and Swift contend on the same lock.** — chose **1.1(a): the run lock is an flock-semantics exclusive lock on a file keyed by run id. Rust takes it with std File::try_lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows; no new crate under rust-core D1), Swift with flock, Node on macOS with fs.openSync(O_EXLOCK|O_NONBLOCK) (verified 2026-09-17 on Node 24.15 to contend with flock, held through SIGSTOP, released on kill -9). Node on Linux holds it through a flock(1) child tied to the driver until sofar-core binaries ship and take over; where flock(1) is absent the driver keeps today's refusal and says liveness cannot be checked. Windows follows sofar-core. Engines floor stays >=18. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over A listening unix socket (blocked by Claude Code's Linux seccomp and macOS Seatbelt sandboxes, stale socket files after kill -9, 104-byte path limit); node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (needs Node >=22.13 and a rusqlite crate on the Rust side, and SQLite's fcntl locks do not see flock on Linux); pid or hostname-pid files; heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile). because rust-core D1 moves status, statusline and hook handlers to Rust while `sofar drive` stays TypeScript, and the Mac app reads through the Rust core, so the lock's readers will be Rust and Swift. flock is the primitive both get with zero new dependencies, and Node can already take the same lock on macOS; the research is in note 01M2QX4KSFFX2QV68YG4QFSKA4.
- 2026-09-17T15:10:01.087Z — rule: **Never write a pid or any content into a run lock file, never place it under the repo, and never unlink it.** — chose **1.1(b): QUALIFIES in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) without overturning it. An empty lock file under the per-user state dir ($XDG_STATE_HOME/sofar or ~/.local/state/sofar), whose liveness answer comes only from whether the OS reports the lock held, is not the pid file D2 forbids. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Reading D2 as forbidding any driver-owned file (leaving no way to tell a live driver from a dead one), or writing a pid into the lock file for diagnostics. because D2's reasons were that a pid is machine-local in a committed log and a reused pid signals a stranger. An empty file outside the repo carries nothing to commit and nothing to reuse: the kernel releases the lock when the holder dies, so no stale value can ever point at another process.

- 2026-09-17T15:10:10.660Z — rule: **Never block a detached or agent-launched run on a keep-awake prompt; prompt only on a TTY, otherwise state the unset setting in the preflight lines.** — chose **1.1(e): keep-awake lives in the engine. Setting `drive.keep_awake` (on/off) in ~/.config/sofar/config.json; a terminal run with the setting unset asks once and saves the answer; a detached or agent-launched run never prompts, and its preflight lines say the setting is unset so the agent asks the operator in chat; `--keep-awake` / `--no-keep-awake` override per run; the opening lines state that idle sleep is blocked but lid-close sleep is not. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Keep-awake only in the paid Mac app (works only while the app runs, and cannot tie itself to the driver's lifetime); always on (surprising power use); a per-repo setting committed to git (sleep is a machine preference, not project state). because Only the driver knows its own lifetime, and `caffeinate -w` ends by itself when the watched process exits, so no cleanup and no pid is stored anywhere. The operator asked for a way to be asked before a run and a setting to turn it on or off.

- 2026-09-22T08:16:15.437Z — chose **2.2 fold shape: RunState gains `adoptions` [{id, ts, epoch}] and `owner` {id, epoch} (run_started's id at epoch 1 until an adoption outranks it), and `stop_requests` now carries event ids instead of envelope timestamps (name unchanged, every other reader used only its length). A stop request is in force when its id sorts after the OWNER's adoption — SPEC's "latest adoption" read as the adoption in force, and SPEC reworded to say so.** over Cutting at the latest adoption by id (a stale lower-epoch adoption synced in late would silence requests meant for the owner); a parallel `stop_request_ids` array beside the timestamps; keeping the wall-clock adoptedAt compare. because Ownership is the highest epoch, not the newest id, so the requests a driver must honour are those made after the adoption that put IT in force. Ids are ulids — they carry the time the timestamps did and every reader of the fold compares the same bytes. Changing the element rather than adding an array keeps one list; rust-core mirrors one line.

- 2026-09-22T13:58:25.036Z — chose **3.1 --await shape: the outcome line goes to stdout (exit 0 stop, exit 2 driver gone); the ABSENT notice and the nothing-to-await refusal (exit 1) go to stderr. The line for a needs_user stop is describeRun plus "<task>'s note: <note>". The note comes from a decode of the log (decodeLines: replay order, corrections voided, same set/clear rule as the fold's blockNotes) at exit. The fold state is left as it was. The driver's byte scan becomes appendedBytesScan(path, from, markers), shared by watchRunEvents and --await.** over Adding blocked-task notes to InitiativeState (a fold shape change that rust-core's fold parity would have to mirror, for a field only --await reads). Parsing current.blocked_on (a '; '-joined string that a note can itself contain). The note is read once, at exit, so a decode there costs nothing per tick and changes nothing Rust mirrors. A tick stays a stat plus a lock probe, which is the "zero cost" the SPEC promises.
- 2026-09-22T14:20:36.239Z — chose **3.2 prompt line gate: "the run moved" means the line minus its liveness word differs from the one this session last saw. That line is `<run> <open|stopped: reason> · <n> handoffs · now on <task> · <done>/<total>`. The mark is kept in <state base>/drive-seen/<clone key>.json and written only on news. The lock is probed only when the line prints. A session the driver launched (SOFAR_DRIVE_NUDGE set) gets no line. The driver's queue (nextTask/queuedTasks) moved to core/drive-queue.ts, and driver/drive.ts re-exports it. The fold keeps no event id per handoff or per task change, so honouring the id would mean a fold shape change that rust-core must mirror, for one line. Also rejected: probing the lock on every prompt to show a driver's death (a flock(1) spawn per prompt on Linux, against D6's no-unconditional-subprocess rule for the hot path), and importing nextTask from driver/drive.ts (it would put the whole driver in the fast.js hook bundle). because The line's own content is exactly what the operator would notice changing. Comparing it needs no new fold state and repeats the line on any lost mark. Measured on the real-record fixture: user-prompt p50 62.3 → 62.7 ms (+0.6%, within r1-fixes D18). In process, a quiet prompt on an open run costs 67 µs and a prompt that prints costs 328 µs. fast.js grows 348.6 → 354.4 KB, with no driver code in it.
- 2026-09-22T14:48:55.356Z — chose **3.3 statusline drive segment, after the record's progress. It reads `drive <task>` while the lock is held, `drive running` when nothing is queued, `drive <task> liveness unknown` with no lock on this machine, `drive gone` with the lock free, and `drive <reason>` for a stop since the session began (no segment when the session is unknown). The `drive` label is dim and the value toned: task cyan, gone red, needs_user yellow, error/stall red, closed green, and max_sessions/cost_cap/interrupted dim. A gone run shows in every session until --resume or --stop. The lock is probed only while a run is open. The pure core is exported as driveSegmentOf(state, sessionStarted, probe), so rust-core has one function to mirror.** over Showing gone only for deaths since the session began (a dead run with no stop blocks a fresh start, so it is always actionable). A glyph for liveness unknown (the statusline laws put words over glyphs, and SPEC's ABSENT rule names the words). Probing on every render regardless of run state. because Tones follow what the stop asks of the operator, within the D1 semantic palette. The done/total the task asks for is already on the record segment beside it, so the segment adds only what is new. D18 against 0.33.0-rc.2 (repo fixture, n=25, interleaved): statusline 62.3 → 62.8 ms (+0.9%), user-prompt +0.9%, stop −0.7%, session-start +4.3% (a path 3.3 does not touch). All within the 10% budget.
